description: Enterprise techniques used by The Gentlemen Ransomware, ATT&CK software S9051 (v1.0)
name: The Gentlemen Ransomware (S9051)

techniques.comment: [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has written registry keys within HKLM and HKCU to gain persistence device wide and to have redundancy.   [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has added registry keys to maintain persistence through `reg add HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v GupdateS /t REG_SZ /d “” /f` and `reg add HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v GupdateU /t REG_SZ /d “” /f`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized the domain’s NETLOGON share to distribute the malicious payload to all domain-joined systems.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized RC scripts to establish persistence in ESXi service.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized PowerShell to execute commands.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also leveraged PowerShell cmdlets to disable real-time monitoring and set exclusions.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized Windows Command Shell to execute commands to facilitate lateral movement and other actions.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized `esxcli` to execute commands on compromised ESXi systems and VMs.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has executed service commands using `sc.exe` to modify configurations and set the service to “start-auto” to run automatically when the system restarted to include `fdrespub`, `fdPHost`, `SSDPSRV` and `upnphost`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has leveraged ephemeral Curve25519 keys with XChaCha20 stream ciphers to encrypt files.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has copied malware executables, such as [PsExec](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0029).exe, to the local `C:\Temp` directory.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) had also enabled a hidden SMB share pointed at the `C:\Temp` folder to allow anonymous access.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also consolidated data in `C:\ProgramData\data\`.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has the ability to change the system’s desktop wallpaper using a bitmap image file stored as `%TEMP%\gentlemen.bmp`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has the functionality to delay for a specified number of minutes before file encryption.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has modified windows firewall rules to allow for discovery actions using `netsh advfirewall firewall set rule group=”Network Discovery” new enable=Yes` and using the PowerShell command `-Command Get-NetFirewall Rule -DisplayGroup “Network Discovery” | Enable-NetFirewallRule`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also modified firewall rules to allow remote desktop access using the command `netsh firewall set service type remotedesktop mode enable` or `netsh advfirewall firewall set rule group="remote desktop" new enable=Yes`.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also deactivated Windows firewall rules using the command ` netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off`. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has disabled the Windows Firewall settings using the PowerShell cmdlet `powershell -Command Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Public,Private -Enabled False`.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has disabled Microsoft Defender utilizing PowerShell commands to include the cmdlet `Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -Force`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also utilized the `TaskKill` command to target specific processes associated with backup software, endpoint detection, and office applications.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has used [Wevtutil](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0645) to clear event logs within system, application and security using the commands `wevtutil cl System`, `wevtutil cl Application`, and `wevtutil cl Security`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized a wipe feature that writes 64 MB chunks of data to a targeted drive to exhaust all free space and overwrites previously deleted file content, reducing recovery capabilities.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has the ability to modify Group Policy on victim Domain Controllers through a PowerShell script that enables simultaneous ransomware detonation on every computer in domain.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has gathered Active Directory domain details utilizing the PowerShell cmdlet `Get-ADDomain`.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has used the following command to re-enable SMB1: `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol -NoRestart`.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized ESXi administration commands to include `vmkfstools` to modify the compromised system.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has enumerated files and directories using WMI and PowerShell commands.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has modified the ownership and access control settings to ensure it has unrestricted write access to target file paths prior to encryption.  [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has leveraged the `takeown`, `icacls` and `attrib` commands to modify permissions on files and folders.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has created hidden SMB share folder named “share$” that allowed anonymous access.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has modified anti-virus settings to add its own executable to the exclusion list of the endpoint detection solution using the PowerShell command `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionProcess  -force`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has deleted PowerShell command history for all users by targeting the command history file located in `C:/Users/*/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Windows/PowerShell/PSReadline/ConsoleHost_History.txt`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has deleted forensic artifacts to include prefetch files, defender diagnostic and support logs using both `del /f /q C:\Windows\Prefetch\*.*` and `del /f /q C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Support\*.*`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) 
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also used a batch script named after itself (`.exe.bat`) to delete [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) and the batch script.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has removed RDP Logs by leveraging the command `del /f /q %SystemRoot%\System32\LogFiles\RDP*\*\*.*`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has deleted Volume Shadow Copies through the use of `vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet` and `wmic shadowcopy delete`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: BradyUnit42_TheGentlemen_July2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also inhibited system recovery by stopping backup services, disabling endpoint protection agents and remote access tools.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has discovered and enumerated valid drives through a PowerShell script.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also scanned for letter drives from A: to Z: using `os.Stat` to determine valid drives.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has deleted preexisting scheduled tasks and created malicious versions of the same named task to execute automatically at system start to include tasks named `UpdateSystem` and `UpdateUser`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also leveraged naming conventions that mimic legitimate VMware services.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has modified registry keys to allow more permissive access controls to include LSA anonymous access controls.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized Windows APIs to facility network share discovery actions.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has discovered and enumerated network shares using `net use` with corresponding sequential drive letters from A through Z.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also enumerated network shares using Windows APIs to include `WnetOpenEnumW`, `WNetEnumResourceW`, and `WNetCloseEnum`.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has obfuscated its code using Go libraries such as `Garble`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has leveraged Base64-encoded PowerShell scripts.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has prevented command logging through the use of `/dev/null 2 &1` that silences output and discards any written data.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized SOCKS proxy connections for C2.(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026)
[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has enabled Remote Desktop Protocol within victim environments.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized SMB to enable lateral movement and file transfers.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has leveraged network shares to distribute the ransomware payload to other victim devices throughout the domain.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has leveraged `crontab` to launch the ransomware after a 60-second delay upon reboot using `echo '@reboot sleep 60 && /bin/.vmware-authd ' | crontab - 2>/dev/null`.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has leveraged scheduled tasks to execute itself as system.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)(Citation: CarveyODonnellWelchHuntress_TheGentlemen_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also established persistence through the creation of scheduled tasks to include `schtasks /Create /SC ONSTART /TN UpdateSystem /TR “” /RU SYSTEM` and `schtasks /Create /SC ONSTART /TN UpdateUser /TR “”`. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has deleted pre-existing scheduled tasks using `schtasks /Delete /TN UpdateSystem /F` and `schtasks /Delete /TN UpdateUser /F`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has excluded the `C:\` volume from scanning to reduce its likelihood of being detected during the encryption process using the PowerShell cmdlet `Add-MpPreference – ExclusionPath C:\ -Force`.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also excluded encryption of specified file names, and file extensions, to include those associated with critical system functionality.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has terminated active processes on the victim device. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has stopped Windows services using `sc config  start=disabled`, `net stop ` and `sc stop `.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also disabled running processes using the `taskkill` command for specified processes.(Citation: TrendAI_TheGentlemen_Sept2025)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has executed service commands using `sc.exe` to modify configurations and allow victim hosts to be visible on the local network.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has conducted clean shutdowns of running VMs in ESXI environments using `vim-cmd vmsvc/power.off  > /dev/null 2>&1`. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also forcibly terminated running VM processes using `esxcli vm process kill --type=force --world-id= > /dev/null 2>&1`.(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)

[The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has utilized wmic to execute commands on victim devices.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026) [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has also leveraged WMI to enumerate volumes and drives.(Citation: MSTI_GentelmenRansomware_May2026)(Citation: CheckPointResearch_TheGentlemen_April2026)
